answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock a non-refundable stake that is slashed the moment it acts dishonestly, making thousands of fake identities prohibitively expensive to spin up. A genuine agent then stands out like a sparrow among forged look-alikes. Attack costs climb until they reach their zenith, while a fraudster's accounts burn out as quickly as a comet streaking across the ledger, leaving only bonded agents that peers can actually trust.
